sentences.text: 3. It appears that an accident of vehicle (Jeep) bearing registration No.JH04C-7291 has taken place on 09.02.2015 and the relative of the claimant(s) has died in that accident.
The deceased was the passenger.
A claim petition has been filed being Claim Case No.30 of 2015 and all the parties have appeared including the owner of the vehicle.

sentences.text: 1 4. The Tribunal, after considering the evidence brought on record, has calculated the amount of compensation and that has not been questioned before this Court by the Insurance Company.
The Insurance Company has questioned only with regard to the existence of the driving license and the permit.

5. It has been submitted that so far as driving license is concerned, as per the FIR, the vehicle in question was driven by Parmeshwar Yadav, but the driving license of Shyam Kishore Yadav has been produced and it is not the driving license of the driver, who was plying the vehicle.
6. From perusal of the record, it appears that both persons have been accepted as same and their identities have also not been questioned by the Insurance Company before the court below.
For the first time, factual dispute has been raised before this Court, which is not acceptable.
Accordingly this plea of the Insurance Company is hereby, denied.

So far as second claim that there was no valid permit for plying the vehicle on the route in question, it has been submitted that in spite of the letter given to the owner of the vehicle, no permit has been produced and then a request has been made before the court below to call for the permit from the owner.
Although the owner has participated in the proceeding, but he has not produced the permit in question.
The nature of the vehicle demands that there has to be permit for plying the same.
Thus, in the absence of permit, the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle.
7. Counsel for the claimant(s) has submitted that he has already received the quantum of compensation and he has no further claim.

8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it appears that the Insurance Company has taken a plea of permit and in spite of the notice and the points taken, the owner of the vehicle has not produced the permit, which is sine qua non for avoidance of the liability.
Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, permits the Insurance Company to avoid the liability on the point of permit, if permit is required.
9. Clearly the nature of the vehicle and the use, suggests that the permit was necessary and in the absence of the permit, the Insurance Company can avoid the liability.

10. In the present case, in spite of the fact that the owner of the vehicle has participated in the proceeding and the permit has been demanded by the Insurance Company, but that has not been produced by the owner of the vehicle.
Thus, adverse inference should have been drawn.
11. In view of the above discussions, the Award dated 27.03.2018 is modified to the extent that the right to recovery is awarded to the Insurance Company.
12. With the above modification in the Award, the present miscellaneous appeal stands disposed of.

13. The statutory amount, if any, shall be remitted, to the Tribunal for release of the same, either in favour of the claimant(s) or the Insurance Company, depending upon the factual matrix of the case.
